security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when Sscsrind is implemented and M-mode firmware leaves mstateen0[60]=0, any KVM host access to vsiselect/vsireg* (or S-mode kernel access to siselect/sireg*) from HS-mode triggers an illegal-instruction exception, crashing the kernel because the trap handler won't expect an illegal-instruction fault on these CSRs in host context.
security_spec.summary: Sscsrind CSR window (siselect/sireg/vsiselect/vsireg) access from HS/S-mode requires mstateen0[60]=1; kernel currently assumes firmware enables this but has no runtime check, risking illegal-instruction panic on non-conformant firmware

findings.finding: KVM host (HS-mode) writes CSR_VSISELECT and reads CSR_VSIREG without checking mstateen0[60]. If Sscsrind is implemented and M-mode firmware leaves mstateen0[60]=0, csr_write(CSR_VSISELECT) triggers illegal-instruction, crashing the host. Expanded via imsic_eix_read() and called from imsic_vsfile_local_read(), imsic_vsfile_local_rw().

KVM host (HS-mode) atomic swap on VSIREG depends on first writing VSISELECT. Same mstateen0[60] dependency. Expanded via imsic_eix_swap() and called from imsic_vsfile_local_read() on VCPU release/migration paths.

KVM host (HS-mode) indirect write via VSISELECT+VSIREG. Expanded via imsic_eix_write(). Called from imsic_vsfile_local_clear() (VCPU migration init) and imsic_vsfile_local_update() (VS-file restore). All depend on mstateen0[60]=1.

KVM host (HS-mode) indirect atomic-set via VSISELECT+VSIREG. Expanded via imsic_eix_set(). Called from imsic_vsfile_local_update() on VS-file restore during VCPU migration. Same mstateen0[60] dependency chain.

VCPU state read/clear from IMSIC VS-file. Saves/restores VSISELECT at lines 380/419 and performs indirect reads via imsic_vs_csr_read/imsic_eix_swap, all depending on mstateen0[60]=1. Called during VCPU release and migration (on_each_cpu_mask cross-call).

Per-VS-file register read/write. Saves/restores VSISELECT at lines 452/487 then performs reads/writes of IMSIC EIDELIVERY/EITHRESHOLD/EIP/EIE via the indirect access macros. Same mstateen0[60] dependency.

Zeroes out a new IMSIC VS-file before use. Saves/restores VSISELECT at lines 529/547, writes zeros via imsic_vs_csr_write and imsic_eix_write. Called from imsic_vsfile_local_clear in kvm_riscv_vcpu_aia_imsic_update() on VCPU migration. mstateen0[60] must be set.

Restores MRIF state into an IMSIC VS-file. Saves/restores VSISELECT at lines 567/586, then uses imsic_eix_set and imsic_vs_csr_write to restore pending/enable/threshold/delivery state. Called on VCPU migration. Same mstateen0[60] dependency.

VCPU load path writes CSR_VSISELECT directly (line 131) or via NACL (line 121) to restore guest vsiselect. This is the hot VCPU-to-CPU binding path executed on every VCPU entry. NACL-wrapped path (lines 119-122) is also vulnerable since the NACL CSR shadow mechanism still depends on mstateen0[60] being set before NACL was initialized.
VCPU put path reads CSR_VSISELECT directly (line 169) or via NACL (line 159) to save guest vsiselect state before VCPU is descheduled. Executed on every VCPU exit. Same mstateen0[60] dependency.

Guest SIREG emulation reads CSR_VSISELECT (line 399) to determine the current iselect value for routing to the correct handler (IPRIO or IMSIC). Called from kvm_riscv_vcpu_aia_rmw_ireg which is registered as the handler for CSR_SIREG in the VCPU CSR dispatch table (kvm_aia.h:148). If VSISELECT read itself faults, the emulation cannot proceed.

KVM sets hstateen0 bits for VS-mode IMSIC access (bits 58-60) via SMSTATEEN0_AIA_IMSIC|SMSTATEEN0_AIA|SMSTATEEN0_AIA_ISEL, but never validates that mstateen0 has these bits set. If mstateen0[60]=0, setting hstateen0[60] is a no-op — the hardware still blocks HS-mode vsiselect/vsireg access. The kernel has no runtime detection of mstateen0 state and no code to detect Sscsrind extension presence.
